observation: Producer/evaluator split caught a genuine security defect the producer missed: the architecture critique flagged that trusting an external MCP server's self-declared idempotentHint is a gate-bypass (a malicious/buggy server marks a destructive op reversible -> runs direct, ungated). Resolution: community (default/unvetted) sources have annotations DROPPED -> fail-closed all-brokered; only vetted sources may downgrade to direct. 8/10 -> 9/10 in one revision round. Evidence the evaluator-different-than-producer boundary pays off on backend WPs too, not just UI.

Load-bearing architecture insight held under code review: 'a brokered call is just a RegisteredTool whose handler runs server-side' rides AL7's existing invoke workflow (classify -> capture -> CAS-consume grant -> execute -> recordOutcome) with ZERO new gate/at-most-once machinery and no kernel-executor reintroduced. tool-registry.ts diff was only the additive ownerUserId field. Reconciled the AN-concept 'Kernel attaches credential' wording with AL7's trust-first no-kernel-executor model without violating either.

Live-proof requirement satisfied in-repo without network/secrets: a real @modelcontextprotocol/sdk McpServer spawned over a real HTTP transport (ephemeral 127.0.0.1 port) + a real stdio child-process server for the second-service-by-config proof. Sanity-break confirmed two load-bearing assertions go RED when reverted (Bearer-token attach -> AC3a red; trustTier vetted gate -> community-companion + forged-hint tests red) -- not green-against-a-mock. The in-repo-server-over-real-transport pattern is a reusable way to meet a live-proof gate inside npm run verify.

TDD red-phase produced first-pass-green code with zero rework rounds: 27 unit + 47 integration AN2 tests green on first full run, all protected AL7/AN1 suites stayed green untouched, code review verdict DONE on the first pass. Backend-only L WP (no /concept, no /design phase) -- the 6-phase pipeline collapsed cleanly to architecture -> critique -> TDD -> review -> docs -> retro.

In-repo McpServer test fixture initially used one shared McpServer + StreamableHTTPServerTransport for all clients; the SDK's stateful mode rejected a second client's initialize with 'Server already initialized'. Fixed in green phase with a per-session McpServer pattern (fresh server+transport per initialize, routed by mcp-session-id header). Cost one extra debug cycle in the green phase. @lore captured. Future MCP-server test fixtures should be per-session from the start.

Minor resource leak found at code review (non-blocking WARNING): connector-resolver enumerates external tools at provision time by connecting out then closing; if listTools() threw after a successful connectOutbound, the connection (and stdio child process) leaked because close() sat inside the try the catch skipped. One-round fix (close on error path + finally-style). Caught by the adversarial lens, not by tests -- resource-lifecycle on error paths is a recurring blind spot tests rarely cover.
